chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-A'la ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
'Beware of speculating about God. But whenever you wish to look upon His Magnificence, then look upon the magnificence of His creation.'

key_terms.التَّفَكُّر: Speculative pondering/contemplation — here referring to unauthorized metaphysical speculation about the divine essence
key_terms.الْخَلْق: Creation — the created universe as a mirror of divine attributes
key_terms.عَظَمَة: Magnificence, Grandeur — referring to the divine attribute of greatness

ai.seo_question: Why does Islam forbid speculating about the nature of God?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) warned against speculative contemplation about the divine essence of God (tafakkur fi Allah), redirecting believers instead to contemplate the grandeur of God's creation as the proper avenue for appreciating divine greatness. This teaching reflects the Shia theological principle that God's essence (dhat) is beyond human comprehension, while His attributes can be witnessed through the created world. The hadith was addressed to disciples who may have been tempted by the theological debates of the era regarding the divine nature.
